elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall...", so all three limbs (assistance, return, deletion) attach to every covered expiry and termination, not merely to anticipated expiry or to Client-elected termination under Section 14.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Client's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — Vendor-side obligation, six-month duration, triggered by a Client request that is available on any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) ends "at TrueLink's then-current rates", matching the playbook pricing basis.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, return to Client all Client Content and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control" — the 30-day clock runs from termination/expiry (not from a request), and the scope is all Client data, not selected categories.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return "in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after such return, delete such Client Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing" — deletion is expressly sequenced after return, avoiding the walk-away outcome of immediate deletion.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same trigger language, "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six months of assistance in limb (a) exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Client data within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination.

reasons: Finding classification is sound: Sections 13-14 contain no data return, export or transition mechanic, and Section 13 imposes only Client-side burdens (new name server within 30 days, new hosting environment within 60 days) plus domain ownership confirmation. Absence of any data return obligation is walk-away territory, so an insertion is warranted.

All six preferred elements are met in the operative inserted text (trigger, six months, then-current rates, 30-day return from termination, standard machine-readable format, certified deletion after return); the fallback is independently met as well.

Minimality holds: the proposal is a single concise insertion into the termination area with no deletions or paraphrase of surrounding language, and it adds no extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no added procedures, no damages or remedy add-ons) beyond what the selected checklist requires. "At Client's request" and "in TrueLink's possession or control" are scope qualifiers consistent with the model language rather than new requirements.

Intent is preserved: Section 13's Client-side name-server and hosting-migration responsibilities, the automatic renewal and non-renewal notice mechanic, Section 14's month-end termination timing and the Section 4/12 cross-references all survive without contradiction; the new clause uses "Client Content", a term already used in Section 13, so no undefined term or dangling reference is created.

Optional housekeeping only (not a defect): the inserted paragraph carries no section number — number it (e.g., Section 15) and confirm it is picked up by any survival provision so the obligations clearly outlive the term.
